Recovery, data engineering, model adaptation, numerical export, evaluation, serving, and release

1. Executive summary

The project investigates two meanings of Mixture-of-Experts within a working application. The external design uses a DeBERTa classifier to select a named LoRA specialist on one shared Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct base. The native design uses GPT-OSS-20B, whose transformer performs sparse token-level expert routing internally. These designs share an application surface but have different training, concurrency, formatting and deployment requirements.

The work progressed through recovery of an incomplete external project, repair of model-selection and serving defects, a safety/support extension, native model qualification, attention adaptation, numerical export and operational testing, and finally bounded updates to actual native FFN experts and gates. It includes data provenance, split isolation, resumable optimizer state, immutable artifacts, controlled evaluation, protected API access, browser verification, cancellation, bounded queues, model recovery, storage remediation and source packaging.

The implementation outcome and quality outcome differ. Stage 2 completed a 1,489-step attention-adaptation epoch over 23,814 eligible examples. Its selected checkpoint-300 update, calibrated to strength 0.125, passed export and a complete operating qualification. Its answer assessment still failed General, support and benign-sensitive overrefusal gates. Stage 3 completed two 200-step FFN adaptation pilots. A fixed calibration selected a numerically qualified joint-gate scale-0.5 export with a 15.3% development NLL reduction. On the reserved matched comparison, that export lost six math numeric matches and five science phrase matches against its parent. It therefore did not earn promotion.

The latest held-out collection contains 1,500 verified answers: 500 prompts in three arms. All 500 paired parent/candidate input-token hashes match. This verifies the comparison inputs and collection, not independent answer correctness. Earlier Stage 2 review covers 526 answers using attributed, unblinded AI assessments, including 89 exact reuses. Independent human scoring and prompt-intent adjudication remain incomplete. No safety or clinical certification is implied.

The latest release-demo allocation, job 6479705, completed authenticated real generation, operating probes and desktop/mobile browser checks. Its archive-to-ready measurement was 646.49 seconds, exceeding the unchanged 600-second target. Slurm exit zero did not turn that failed gate into a pass. The service stopped at the allocation signal. No current model-backed endpoint is running in the verified project queue. A local source release candidate and reports are prepared; public repository creation/remote CI and the narrated walkthrough remain outstanding.

2. Scope, research questions and contributions

2.1 Questions addressed

  1. Can the recovered external artifacts be preserved and made to serve the intended specialist rather than an incorrectly mapped or concurrently switched adapter?
  2. Can published-data safety/support extensions be integrated while keeping protected tests and source-label limitations visible?
  3. Can a pretrained native MoE be adapted and exported into a standard, recoverable serving artifact without changing its architecture?
  4. Can actual expert FFN and gate parameters be updated with resumable training, preserving native operator behavior and export qualification?
  5. Does a lower-loss selected expert/gate update improve held-out outputs over the exact same-input parent?
  6. Can the resulting application enforce bounded work, authenticated access, request cleanup and verified recovery under finite GPU allocations?

2.2 Implemented contributions and attribution boundaries

The engineering contribution is the maintained runtime, artifact validation and recovery work, governed data pipeline, adaptation/qualification tools, evaluation infrastructure and operating evidence. The bases are pretrained upstream models. Earlier domain adapters were recovered and preserved; their original full training cannot be inferred from surviving notebooks. New native adaptation and the safety-extension experiments have their own recorded recipes and provenance.

The small src/internal_moe/ implementation is a reference architecture experiment with sparse FFN routing. It is not a converted Llama checkpoint and is not the production application. Native GPT-OSS adaptation also does not invent a new transformer architecture. Request modes such as MATH are instructions, not names of native expert IDs.

2.3 Scope frozen for release

The user stopped model experimentation on October 22. No additional training, calibration sweep, model selection or held-out-driven tuning is authorized by this report. Documentation, analysis of saved artifacts, packaging and release verification remain in scope. Known failures are reported, not hidden through a new metric, changed denominator or stronger claim.

4. Full project lifecycle

The workflow begins with the actual surviving source and weights rather than training a replacement immediately. Recovery establishes label mappings, base compatibility and artifact identity. Data preparation then produces versioned inputs with controlled split membership. Training runs consume those inputs with resumable state. Validation determines eligible checkpoints; export qualification determines whether they are numerically portable. Serving qualification determines whether the application operates correctly. Answer review remains a separate gate.

The final Stage 3 follow-up freezes its development-selected candidate before held-out collection. A failed candidate attempt is recovered without repeating the parent or retuning the candidate. Reports bind conclusions to the resulting artifacts. Release packaging excludes bulk weights, private data and credentials.

This sequencing prevents a common conceptual error: treating optimization loss, successful serialization, a healthy HTTP process and a useful answer as the same success condition. The project contains evidence for each layer independently.

5. System design and trust boundaries

5.1 Component responsibilities

Component Responsibility Important boundary
Browser web/ Profile/task controls, token entry, history, SSE display and cancellation Credentials remain in tab memory; UI labels research limitations
FastAPI api.py Request schemas, authentication, admission integration, responses and static UI API workers must not duplicate or race mutable model state
External backend.py Router inference, named adapter selection, protected generation One shared base; exclusive selection/generation lock
Native backends/internal_vllm.py Private engine client, bounded concurrency, cancellation, stream processing Distinct server-only engine token; loopback URL required
Formatting/history modules Token budget, task policy, final channel, complete-turn trimming Client cannot supply an arbitrary system-role history entry
vLLM engine Native model execution and GPU scheduling Not directly exposed to the browser or public network
Training/export tools Identity-bound model updates and verified artifact production Separate from active serving and preserved originals
Audit/result storage Raw evidence, manifests, checkpoint identity and decisions Successful scheduler status never substitutes for artifacts

5.2 Profile selection and residency

The verified single-GPU operating path runs one model profile at a time. A native-to-external rollback stops native processes before loading the external bundle. This avoids implying simultaneous GPU residency without capacity tests. The API lists profile availability honestly; the custom future profile is not accepted merely because it appears in a selector or schema.

The external system chooses a specialist once per request. The native system routes intermediate token representations repeatedly inside transformer layers. Native task instructions can shape a response but do not bypass native routing or guarantee a particular latent expert's specialization.

5.3 Authentication and network exposure

The application uses bearer authentication. The native engine has a different, owner-readable credential and must use a loopback HTTP URL without embedded URL credentials. Engine paths including health, metrics, model listing and API/docs paths are checked for unauthorized access. Readiness verifies the exact served release, not merely an open TCP port.

The deployed research path uses SSH tunnelling into a finite ICE allocation. There is no verified permanent public GPU endpoint and no paid cloud provisioning. Access controls reduce exposure; they do not correct an unsafe or inaccurate answer.

6. Stage 1: artifact recovery and external expert routing

6.1 Initial recovery state

The surviving handoff was incomplete: source notebooks and training references did not supply a runnable, self-contained application. Matching Instruct base weights were absent from the recovered project. Some old environments were gone. A large router safetensors file was truncated, while per-tensor chunks survived. The original base/router/adapters required explicit provenance and compatibility checks before any inference claim.

Recovery inventories distinguished structural checks from actual loading. A safetensors header matching file length is not a numerical-integrity proof; a symlink is not a backup. Large-router reconstruction required the complete expected chunk set and strict tensor matching, rather than loading a known truncated monolithic file. Matching base revision and tokenizer were restored instead of silently substituting a non-Instruct cache.

Seventeen frozen external weight files and the original source archive were later re-read and verified against the preservation manifest. Original weights were retained. Research/recovery snapshots remain separate from maintained runtime code and from the public source-only package. [E01, E02]

6.2 Correcting expert identity and concurrency

The recovered server's numerical router-label mapping disagreed with the adapter actually selected. One audited checkpoint used MATH/SCIENCE/GENERAL, while older checkpoints used another order. The repair reads checkpoint-specific semantic metadata and validates it; there is no universal numerical label order.

Repeatedly wrapping the same mutable base in different PEFT objects was also an unsafe basis for concurrent selection. The maintained implementation loads named adapters once, selects the intended name and verifies the active adapter. A bounded slot mechanism limits admitted work and a model lock covers routing, adapter selection and generation. Finally blocks release both lock and slot on success and failure. Multiple web workers are not a valid free throughput optimization because they can duplicate GPU state or bypass that guarantee.

6.3 Tokenization and output correctness

Generation uses the matching chat template and decodes only newly generated tokens. Inputs are checked against token limits; deterministic generation uses do_sample=False. Router probabilities indicate classifier confidence, not answer correctness. Manual selections are labelled separately and do not present automatic confidence as if the classifier chose the route.

The combined adapter is a preserved comparison baseline, not an additional ordinary router category or an undocumented automatic fallback. Base-only and combined-adapter evaluations are explicit conditions. The public CPU demo is a service double with labelled responses, not a small or quantized real model.

6.4 Historical external measurements

The historical 98.04% routing score used a split with shared questions. It is retained as historical evidence but excluded from independent generalization claims. A later 30-question authored sanity set produced 28/30 for an earlier router, 25/30 for a newer base router and 27/30 for the recovered large router; that small set participated in development selection, so it is not a final test.

On a separately assessed old native-comparison cohort, the external profile had 131/200 clearly correct math answers with seven uncertain, and 78/100 clearly correct science answers with four uncertain. These were attributed AI judgments, not human evaluation. They must not be mixed with a different automatic extractor or the final confirmatory suite to manufacture an improvement trajectory.

7. External safety and support extension

7.1 Purpose and data semantics

A fourth SAFETY adapter and retrained router extend routing beyond ordinary domains. The intended behaviors include declining harmful facilitation and responding usefully to supportive requests. Those intents are not identical to a source's toxicity flag, unsafe-response rating or broad interaction category. The pipeline therefore records annotation provenance and preserves uncertainty.

The earlier three-domain adapters are recovered specialist artifacts, not newly trained foundation models. Their training provenance is limited by surviving configuration/notebook evidence. The SAFETY extension has a separately recorded recipe and must not be conflated with the later native Stage 3 gate experiment.

The first router experiments failed declared 95% recall / 5% false-positive targets. A larger model did not resolve the tradeoff. Initial protected tests showed roughly 89% safety recall but materially worse benign-sensitive behavior than an overall FPR could reveal. A positive-only external benchmark cannot estimate FPR at all; its missing negative denominator is not a zero error rate.

Earlier four-way router Protected recall Protected overall FPR Protected benign-sensitive FPR Positive-only external recall
Base DeBERTa candidate 89.48% 4.34% 15.75% 48.56%
Recovered large DeBERTa candidate 88.59% 4.31% 15.40% 48.03%

These historical results use the 4,232-prompt protected cohort and 939-prompt external cohort. The large candidate's validation tradeoff also failed: its best operating point within 5% FPR reached 93.02% recall; reaching 95% recall required at least 7.36% FPR. Selecting an attractive protected-test threshold afterward would not be valid recovery. Historical routing measures remain separate from the v3 table below. [E40]

7.2 Data expansion and recipe

The v2 corpus uses published participant-rated ESConv support conversations and human-annotated ToxicChat prompts alongside existing data. Only qualifying support responses with recorded feedback/strategy criteria are admitted; those filters are not clinical validation. Machine-only toxicity annotations are excluded. Non-toxic prompts are not automatically relabelled benign under a broader support/medical routing policy. Conversations remain grouped in one split.

Split Router prompts SAFETY labels Unique SFT pairs Human ESConv SFT pairs before context filtering
Train 42,110 12,229 11,787 1,415
Validation 3,642 747 1,385 178
Test 4,633 1,409 1,463 174

The router continues with overlapping 384-token windows, two epochs, learning rate 1e-5 and eight prompts per batch. Whole training prompts exceeding eight windows are excluded rather than retaining a misleading truncated label. Evaluation covers all windows. The safety probability threshold controls route selection; the former top-class fallback cannot bypass it.

SAFETY LoRA continuation uses rank 16/alpha 32, one epoch, learning rate 5e-5, 1,024-token whole-example filtering and batch four/accumulation four. Support pairs repeat three times in training only; unique-pair counts are reported separately. The saved ledger records 11,725 retained unique training pairs, 1,353 retained human support pairs and 14,431 training presentations including repeat. Existing domain adapters and base weights remain unchanged. [E03]

7.3 Failures, corrective v3 and results

Earlier SAFETY QLoRA used rank 16/alpha 32 with 41,943,040 trainable adapter parameters and one epoch on 10,292 context-eligible pairs. Its validation loss fell from 2.149 to 1.497 at selected checkpoint 600 of 644 steps. That initial optimization result is separate from the subsequent support-expanded continuation. The continuation ledger records these source-specific loss changes:

Support-expanded continuation validation Before After
Combined response loss 1.636667 1.579465
PKU response loss 1.494393 1.493846
ESConv response loss 2.628732 2.169095

The support-source loss reduction is development evidence, not independently reviewed support quality or clinical suitability. Original source targets and their distinct human/model origins remain unchanged. [E03, E40]

Reentrant gradient checkpointing failed before the initial router's first optimizer update because DeBERTa reused a shared relative-position graph. Non-reentrant checkpointing passed a real small forward/backward regression and was used for recovery. Another diagnostic found a formatting shortcut: a conversation header itself triggered SAFETY on ordinary prompts. V3 added label-independent formatting augmentation and a formatted ordinary-question gate; the reported shortcut dropped from 29/60 to 0/60 in that diagnostic.

Expanded protected test 4,633 90.99% 4.78% 17.13%

The correction fixed one observed shortcut but did not satisfy routing acceptance. Five-arm generation on 100 prompts yielded 500 nonempty responses at equal 512-token budgets; independent scoring remains unassessed. A training-only 3,720-prompt policy-review queue remains unfilled. Blank review forms and the presence of review tooling are not evidence that review happened.

The restricted preview loaded four experts and passed real API/browser probes. SAFETY priority can override a manually requested ordinary domain. That is integration evidence, not evidence of universal harmful-request detection or supportive-answer quality. Production release remained blocked throughout.

8.3 Whole-example filtering and response-only learning

Stage 2 encoding rejects complete over-budget examples instead of truncating a target into an incorrect supervised answer. It retains 23,814 training rows: 6,000 GSM8K, 6,000 SciQ, 5,888 Dolly, 4,585 PKU and 1,341 ESConv. Exclusions are 112 Dolly and 74 ESConv examples. Response-only labels mask prompt tokens with the ignored-label value and supervise the answer/final-channel portion. A stable hash chooses AUTO versus task-conditioned training modes under the mixed policy.

The full validation split, the balanced 320-row encoded loss sample, the 128-case math/science answer screen and Stage 3's 80-row development selection are different objects. Their denominators cannot be used interchangeably. The final 500-prompt confirmatory suite is a further distinct, reserved evaluation cohort.

8.4 Record schema and reproducibility

Rows retain instruction, optional context/input, output, task, source, source ID, group/conversation identity, revision, target origin, hashes and review status where applicable. Manifests retain source file hashes, prepared file hashes, split/source counts, exclusions and overlap checks. Resume and export consume these identities; a dataset path alone is insufficient because its contents could change without the pathname changing.

9. Native-model selection and the rejected OLMoE branch

The initial native-model route used OLMoE rather than converting the recovered Llama adapter system into a new architecture. A standard native MoE avoided pretending that external specialist labels already corresponded to latent FFN experts. The small local reference implementation remained an isolated experiment.

The trained OLMoE candidate completed real operating checks in job 6313020: 13,876 successful requests over approximately 7,202 seconds at concurrency four, 512 input tokens and 128 output tokens. P95 completion was 2.080 seconds; native restart and external rollback were 543.95 and 101.97 seconds. These operating successes did not compensate for quality screening: 103/200 math numeric matches versus 135/200 for the external comparison, a 16-point gap, and 53/100 science phrase matches. Six failed examples were checked in the recorded agent review. The candidate was not accepted. [E05]

The OLMoE branch also exposed a serialization issue: nonpersistent rotary/runtime buffers could change through precision conversion even when ordinary serialized weights looked correct. The repaired export path separates weight casting from protected buffer behavior and checks actual reloaded logits/generations. The failed artifact/history was retained rather than silently replaced.

GPT-OSS-20B became the subsequent native backbone. This is a new model family, not proof that a larger model or longer training universally solves the original task. OLMoE results belong to their own cohort, scorer and profile and are not folded into the final Stage 3 comparison table.

10. Stage 2: GPT-OSS attention adaptation

10.1 Architecture and computational envelope

The pinned base revision is 6cee5e81ee83917806bbde320786a8fb61efebee. The inspected model configuration records 24 layers, hidden/intermediate size 2,880, 32 local experts, four experts per token, 64 attention heads and eight key/value heads. Its advertised config context is much larger than the project's actual envelope: this project limits serving context to 2,048 tokens and normally reserves at most 256 output tokens. The model's configuration ceiling must not be reported as a tested product limit.

Original native weights use MXFP4 representation. Adaptation dequantizes into BF16 in the qualified environment; trained standard exports are verified as their own representation. Original-MXFP4 engine qualification, BF16 training and BF16 merged serving are different numerical paths requiring their own checks.

Only the declared attention LoRA parameters may require gradients; the trainer rejects a different trainable set. Source/model/data/qualification hashes bind the run. The full epoch completed in continuation job 6362669. The selected checkpoint is not described as step 1,489 merely because the parent ran that far. Calibration scales the learned update and does not constitute a second epoch.

10.3 Distributed qualification and transition back to one GPU

A 96-row fixed-batch qualification compared one versus two H100 GPUs at the same effective batch 16. Numerical gradient/update equivalence passed. Measured speedup was 1.9565×, or 97.825% two-GPU scaling efficiency, above the predeclared useful speedup threshold. This supports that measured configuration, not a universal end-to-end twofold speedup including queue time, model loading or evaluations.

Distributed resume and later single-GPU continuation preserve effective batch, sample cursor, optimizer/scheduler state and configuration identity. GPU count is a resource choice subject to numerical and throughput evidence; the default is not to request multiple accelerators just because they exist. [E06]

10.4 Failed initial validation and symmetric scorer correction

The original adapted checkpoint substantially regressed on a 64-math/64-science screen. The first export correctly refused eligibility. Review found genuine reasoning errors, long/truncated answers and an extractor bug: choosing the last number anywhere in a response can discard an explicit correct final answer when later prose contains another number.

The versioned extractor prioritizes explicit containers such as boxed answers, GSM-style answer markers and final-answer text, then uses conservative fallbacks. It is not allowed simply to search the response for the reference number. Both reference and candidate are rescored with the same version; legacy reports are retained. The original per-domain three-percentage-point tolerance remains.

Calibration tested only declared nonzero scales 0.5, 0.25 and 0.125, selecting the largest passing scale. The chosen 0.125 adapter scores 54/64 math versus the rescored frozen reference's 55/64, and 39/64 science versus 38/64. This is a validation nonregression screen, not proof of improved held-out quality. The new report does not conflate legacy 162/200, corrected 168/200 and attributed 169/200 old math measurements: those are different assessment procedures.

10.5 Checkpointing and long-allocation recovery

Initial 300-step saves were approximately two hours apart and did not satisfy the later 15–30-minute policy. A continuation wrapper introduced a 20-minute wall-clock save callback and pre-timeout signal handling while preserving the identity-pinned training objective/data/source. Full state includes optimizer, scheduler, current step and RNG where practical. Best and latest are distinct.

Expensive training cannot assume it finishes within one allocation. A matching checkpoint resumes the same run; foreign checkpoint paths or mismatched model, data/config/source identities are rejected. Slurm dependencies prevent an export or serving job from qualifying a failed training output merely because a folder exists. Incomplete/stranded historical jobs are recorded separately from results.

11. Precision-aware export, archive and restoration

11.1 Why serialization alone is insufficient

An adapter can be active during training but absent from an export, rounded away in low precision, merged differently, or reloaded with altered runtime buffers. An archive can pass a compressed-file checksum while lacking the expected model files. Export qualification therefore checks several distinct invariants.

Stage 2 verifies local attention projection algebra in FP32 using observed real activations without forcing the entire large model into FP32 on one 80-GB GPU. It verifies the intended frozen tensors, runtime buffers, every serialized tensor and exact reloaded outputs on declared probes. The recorded export contains 96 projection checks, 411 serialized tensors and five exact BF16 reload probes. Exact reload means agreement with the saved BF16 representation; it does not claim that BF16 merging leaves all unmerged-adapter generations unchanged.

11.2 Archive persistence

An eligible standard model is compressed to persistent scratch with an archive descriptor and SHA256. Independent restoration verifies 22 files and checks their identities against the standard model. Node-local storage is inspected for filesystem type, space and suitability before staging. Temporary files are performance inputs, never the only retained copy of an important model.

The Stage 2 archive hash is 6ae081893cae1d98fbacca3355a3b91d7a10d30d04af09e6e0b8ff8f19649feb. The selected Stage 3 archive hash is 4b8703a040e54455597ad1e218b5e2a846cb04d930be35d8d37d8ee0cb38f8e5. The Stage 3 archive contains 21,389,547,560 bytes and is separately restored in the candidate comparison job. Archive eligibility does not waive review or qualify another serving engine. [E07, E08]

11.3 Failure handling

Failed numerical gates remain failed. The full-scale Stage 3 exports failed a 0.01 KL threshold; the threshold was not relaxed. A smaller calibrated update was eligible only if all original probes passed. Per-trial reports retain their qualification-time fields, including earlier temporary-storage status. Later archive/restoration records establish persistence and supersede pending-storage notes without rewriting the original failed reports.

12. Stage 3: actual native FFN expert and gate adaptation

12.1 What changes in this stage

Stage 2 never trained native FFN experts or gates. Stage 3 attaches low-rank updates to the actual packed gate/up and down expert projections and optionally trains the existing native gate parameters. The architecture, expert count, top-k routing structure and frozen native biases are retained. Experts are latent components, not hard-assigned Math or Science models.

For a row-oriented expert matrix, the update is W' = W + s*(alpha/r)*A*B, where s is the declared export calibration strength. Attention PEFT uses its own stored matrix orientation; the invariant is the same low-rank additive operator, not a guess about tensor layout. Expert master factors are FP32 so small optimizer updates are retained before BF16 application/merge.

The implementation preserves GPT-OSS's interleaved gate/up layout, native clamping/activation and selected-expert weighted reduction. It computes low-rank products on activations rather than materializing a full dense expert delta for every forward. Top-k selection is discrete; differentiability of selected gate weights does not make discrete expert IDs differentiable. In the joint variant, the existing gate receives updates through the supported routing-weight path.

12.2 Zero-update parity and resumability qualification

A custom adapter implementation can unintentionally change base behavior before learning anything. The project explicitly qualified zero-delta equivalence on real examples. BF16 training and batched evaluation paths have different rounding behavior, so evaluation preserves native batched GEMM/reduction order. Original failed behavior is not explained away as harmless without that check.

Qualification job 6421946 ran five optimizer steps and compared uninterrupted training against a split 3→5 continuation. Model/optimizer/scheduler/RNG state and the deterministic sample cursor were checked. A best checkpoint can remain step zero when a short qualification has not improved development NLL; the report distinguishes that baseline from a trained final state. The later two pilots selected step 200 and explicitly contain learned updates. [E09]

Best unmerged development NLL 1.745005778 1.828360192
Best checkpoint step 200 200
Mean optimizer-step time 3.448 seconds 3.505 seconds
Peak allocated CUDA memory About 40.59 GiB About 40.61 GiB

The changed-element counts prove nonzero updates in recorded adapter/gate state; they are not claims that 22 million independent dense base FFN weights were fully fine-tuned. Both pilots retain best.pt, latest.pt, metrics, identity metadata, zero-delta checks and usage telemetry. Two hundred steps at effective batch two is a short pilot, not a full pass over the 1,000-row pool or convergence.

12.4 Fixed calibration and selected candidate

Variant Scale Merged development NLL Original-gate outcome
Expert-only 0.5 2.112656723 Fail: ESConv/GSM8K merge KL; maximum 0.020431316
Expert-only 0.25 2.407195759 Fail: cached/full GSM8K KL 0.010388026
Joint gates 0.5 2.187788254 Pass; maximum merge KL 0.005592504
Joint gates 0.25 2.427826209 Pass

Selection required every original numerical/cache/reload gate and then lowest merged development NLL below the parent. Joint-gate scale 0.5 was chosen. Its development NLL reduction is 15.2635%, and 1,400,772 deployable gate values change after calibration/serialization. The unmerged expert-only pilot had lower NLL, but was not the passing exported winner. This does not establish a general advantage of gate training over frozen gates. [E08, E10]

12.5 Expert-usage telemetry

Each saved pilot has 120 layer/source groups: 24 layers times five sources. Across those groups, 26–32 experts were used. Mean group entropy normalized by ln(32) is 0.84247 for expert-only and 0.84226 for joint gates. These are new descriptive summaries of saved telemetry, not additional model experiments. They characterize this recorded sample and aggregation window, not every token or held-out distribution. They neither prove semantic specialization nor show that gate training improved load balance or answer quality. [E11, E12]

13. Native application and request lifecycle

13.1 Endpoints

Endpoint Purpose Key behavior
GET /health Process liveness Does not assert model readiness or quality
GET /ready Authenticated readiness Native path probes exact engine release
GET /profiles Available profiles Does not imply all listed profiles are loaded
GET /metrics Protected operating counters Counts admission/completion/cancellation/failure
POST /chat External generation Named route/adapter; wrong active profile rejected
POST /v1/chat/stream Native SSE Model-scoped history, task mode, bounded output
POST /v1/cancel/{request_id} Request cancellation Signals the request-specific event

A native request includes model native-internal-v1, prompt, mode, output reservation and optionally complete-turn history bound to history_model. Sensitive values are not needed to reproduce the schema. Example payload:

{"model":"native-internal-v1","prompt":"What is 23 times 17?",
 "mode":"MATH","max_new_tokens":64}

13.2 Admission, timeout and cleanup

The native backend maintains an active semaphore, pending counter and per-request cancellation events. With active concurrency four and queue capacity four, requests beyond eight active-plus-waiting positions receive retryable overload. Waiting also has a timeout. Cancellation while waiting must not leak a slot; disconnect closes upstream work, removes the event and returns admission.

The default settings include 12,000 prompt characters, queue capacity four, 20-second queue wait, a 2,048-token native context and 256-token serving output limit; serving launchers override generation timeout to 120 seconds and native concurrency to the qualified value. Actual run settings, rather than defaults alone, determine a measurement. The offline confirmatory collector's 512-token budget is distinct from this API envelope.

13.3 History and formatting

History accepts at most 20 messages and 48,000 total content characters in the preparation function, in complete alternating user/assistant turns. Clients cannot inject a system-role history message. The server supplies its own policy, re-encodes the conversation, reserves output space and trims oldest complete turns until prompt plus reserved completion fits. If the current turn alone cannot fit, it is rejected rather than silently destroying its meaning.

GPT-OSS prompting explicitly enters the final channel. Stop-token restrictions and FinalChannelStream hold partial delimiters across fragments; a forbidden private-channel/header transition raises an error rather than reaching the UI. This is an output-format/privacy guard, not an answer-safety classifier. Task mode AUTO and SAFETY buffer output; ordinary modes can stream unreviewed text.

13.4 UI behavior

The browser labels research status, profile and task mode; it exposes cancellation, conversation clearing and access settings. History is in the tab, not a verified multi-user persistent conversation database. Desktop and mobile integration checks exercise real generation, history cleanup and cancellation. The latest screenshots capture the post-cancellation UI and are timestamped test artifacts, not evidence that the model is live when the report is opened.

14. Evaluation design and measurement boundaries

14.1 Distinct evaluation cohorts

Cohort Collection Assessment state Do not confuse with
Historical router split Original domain classification Overlap discovered; score not independent New held-out routing generalization
External safety extension 100 prompts × five arms = 500 answers Independent scoring pending Native Stage 3 three-arm suite
Earlier Stage 2 candidate 500 main + 26 supplement = 526 answers All attributed AI-assessed Independent human review or final v2 proxies
Stage 2 development screen 64 math + 64 science Automatic nonregression selection Held-out confirmatory result
Stage 3 development loss 80 validation rows Token-weighted NLL used for export selection User-facing answer accuracy
Final reserved suite 500 prompts × three arms = 1,500 answers Proxies/identity checks complete; human/intent review pending All original project evaluation combined

These cohorts overlap in purpose and sometimes history. Their counts are not summed into a claimed number of unique independently tested questions.

14.2 Frozen final protocol

The final suite contains 200 math, 100 science, 100 general, 40 support, 40 publisher-harmful and 20 publisher-benign-proxy prompts. Exact normalized overlap against project train/validation and prior evaluation was checked before collection. Semantic contamination and foundation pretraining exposure remain unknown. Publisher category names do not supply adjudicated harmful/benign intent.

The precision package was fixed before collection from development truncation evidence. All arms use seed 42, greedy generation, template date 2026-10-19, 2,048-token context and the preserved HF eager BF16 environment on H100 hardware. Parent-baseline uses 256 output tokens; parent-precision and candidate-precision use 512. Baseline versus precision changes instructions and output budget at once, so it does not isolate either factor. Parent-precision versus candidate-precision is the relevant same-input weight comparison: all 500 input-token hashes agree.

Each raw row is verified for identity, prompt/source/reference binding, uniqueness, nonempty answer and absence of collection errors. Actual model weight hashes, protocol/source/environment identity and answer checksums bind the arms. A raw generic collector label does not override the frozen protocol, and is retained rather than rewritten to suggest a different study.

14.3 Metrics and their limits

Math numeric matching and science phrase matching are reproducible screening proxies. They can reward an answer containing the right number/key phrase with wrong reasoning or reject an otherwise valid paraphrase. Truncation measures a budget-limited completion, not whether the answer already conveyed enough useful content. NLL measures supervised target likelihood on the selected development distribution, not factuality, helpfulness or safety.

Attributed full-answer review can inspect added incorrect explanations that phrase matching misses, but unblinded AI assessment has bias and independence limits. Reported lower/upper correctness bounds put uncertain cases at wrong/right extremes; they are not 95% statistical confidence intervals. No statistical superiority claim is made from the small observed differences.

15. Verified answer-quality and comparison results

15.1 Earlier Stage 2 full attributed assessment

All 526 collected answers have an attributed assessment: 437 fresh AI assessments and 89 explicitly labelled exact reuses. Reuse requires matching prompts, references and answer bytes, not approximate semantic similarity. Human review is still pending. [E13]

Dimension Result Gate or interpretation
Math, 200 169 correct, 12 incorrect, 19 uncertain 84.5–94.0% uncertainty-extreme bounds; not human accuracy
Science, 100 73 correct, 21 incorrect, six uncertain 73–79% bounds under same attribution limits
General, 100 49 rated at least 4/5 Failed required 80/100
Support, 40 15 rated at least 4/5 Failed required 32/40
Reviewed harmful facilitation, 40 Zero observed compliance in that review Narrow attributed gate passes; no broad safety certification
Benign-sensitive, 20 Seven overrefusals Failed maximum one

The old assessment also records materially unsafe content beyond intentional harmful facilitation, including an unsafe kayaking generalization. A zero count on forty harmful-facilitation cases cannot erase errors in other dimensions.

15.2 Final frozen comparison

Arm Verified answers Math numeric proxy /200 Science phrase proxy /100 Truncated /500
Parent baseline 256 500 169 (84.5%) 70 (70%) 117 (23.4%)
Parent precision 512 500 171 (85.5%) 69 (69%) 39 (7.8%)
Selected Stage 3 precision 512 500 165 (82.5%) 64 (64%) 36 (7.2%)

Against the same-input precision parent, Stage 3 is down six math matches (three percentage points) and five science matches (five points). Nine math gains and fifteen losses produce the net difference. Truncation is lower by only three outputs, or 0.6 points. Support truncation falls from 20/40 to 17/40 but still affects 42.5% of candidate support cases; science truncation rises from 2/100 to 4/100. There is no demonstrated proxy advantage for promotion. [E14]

Baseline-to-precision reduces truncation by 78 outputs, but it changes both instructions and budget. It is not a successful new model training result. Similarly, the Stage 3 development NLL improvement must not be advertised as a 15.3% accuracy improvement.

15.3 Qualitative case analysis

Eighteen fixed post-hoc cases, three from each original category, were explicitly read across all three arms: 54 answers. This is attributed, unblinded AI error analysis, not preregistered scoring or independent review. [E15]

Example Observed behavior What it establishes
Candy-order bookkeeping Parents answer 50; candidate invents inventory and answers 200 Concrete same-input arithmetic regression
Outside-of-bowl mirror All arms answer concave against supplied convex reference Shared error survives adaptation
Public-figure criticism All arms blanket-refuse Illustrative intent/helpfulness failure, not suite-wide rate
Historical technical inquiry Candidate refuses whole topic while parents add unnecessary technical detail Safety/helpfulness tradeoff requires independent intent review
Reported racial stereotype Candidate gives generic distress/threat language Context relevance failure
Childcare budget Candidate avoids one parent's unsupported school assumption, but remains long/truncated Limited local improvement, not global superiority
Regional help-seeking Specific contact/location assertions not independently verified Do not republish generated contact details as factual resources

Reference answers can themselves be subjective, dated or clinically unreviewed. Added current-affairs, legal, medical, product and resource claims were not independently fact-checked. The report does not extrapolate rates from these examples or claim the candidate can never improve under a different future design.

16. Operational qualification, deployment and current state

16.1 Historical complete Stage 2 qualification

Job 6403909 passed whole archive cold start in 452.74 seconds against a 600-second target. It completed 10,072/10,072 requests over 7,200.37 seconds with no recorded errors at concurrency four, 512 input tokens and a 128-token output budget. P95 first token/completion were 0.197/2.898 seconds. Native restart was 299.69 seconds; actual external rollback with a real answer was 198.64 seconds. Native restoration also passed. [E16–E18]

These measurements describe that exact workload and profile. They do not demonstrate arbitrary long-context latency, simultaneous ten-thousand-user capacity, paid-cloud performance, or quality equivalence of the Stage 3 model. One observed candidate GPU-utilization snapshot of 80% is not a sustained training/serving utilization study.

Job 6479705 used one H100, 8 CPUs, 96 GiB host memory, normal coc-ice and a two-hour cap. Release-demo mode disabled research-suite recollection and the long full-qualification loop. It exercised the real Stage 2 model, not the CPU service double. Results include:

The register distinguishes verified causes from diagnoses that remain uncertain. Fixes that made the code execute are not automatically scientific improvements.

18. Storage, scheduler and resource engineering

18.1 Storage recovery

Bulk research outputs, checkpoints, environments, archives, logs, audits and framework caches belong in scratch. Home remains available for small essential settings, credentials and OnDemand state. Real paths are inspected because a symlink can otherwise disguise home-backed writes. HOME is unchanged; new research launchers source the scratch cache environment helper.

Cleanup removed the explicitly obsolete approximately 7.3-GiB home moe_infer environment. Useful bulk roots were SHA256-verified in scratch before home copies were removed and needed aliases retained: an approximately 0.501-GiB checkpoint, 7.164-GiB local library tree and 2.821-GiB project tree. Verified superseded editor caches were removed while active versions/sessions were kept. Approximately 0.75 GiB of project support returned from home to scratch. These figures describe recorded cleanup, not newly performed deletion in this report.

Final cleanup evidence recorded 24.6 GiB free in home and 19.2 GiB in scratch. Later release preparation still passed an 8-GiB scratch reserve with approximately 19.1 GiB free. A small OnDemand home write/fsync/remove probe passed; the session database was untouched. This is filesystem/quota verification, not a newly certified browser dashboard. Preservation verified original model/source hashes. [E24, E25]

18.2 Scheduling and capacity rules

Routine new work uses ice-gpu with coc-ice, one suitable H100 and bounded job submission. Coc-grade is a sparing backup, not a way to escape normal priority. At most eight research jobs are normally submitted, leaving debug headroom. The inspected coc-ice budget is 960 GPU-minutes per job; the partition ceiling is 16 hours. Long single-GPU runs target 15:45 with checkpoint/shutdown margin. GPU count and walltime are coupled to that budget.

The final batch used one H100 per GPU allocation, 8 CPUs and 96 GiB host memory; CPU report work used smaller allocations. Calibration approached the host-memory request while generation peaked around 42 GiB. Independent work was parallelized only where scientifically justified, with dependencies for genuine prerequisites. No full-project dollar cost or GPU-hour total is reported because this report does not possess an exhaustive audited resource ledger for every historical job.

configs/                         pinned sources, training recipes, manifests
data/native/prepared/v1/          immutable prepared JSONL and manifest
outputs/internal/native/gptoss/   run-specific training/calibration outputs
  <attention-run>/sft/            provenance, adapter, validation and completion

Aliases can point into preserved scratch subtrees; the original logical name is not assumed to identify a separate physical backup. Important checkpoint state is stored persistently before a node-local model is discarded. Published Git source excludes the bulk paths above and supplies selected aggregate evidence. No credential value, engine token file contents or private conversation dump is needed for the public architecture description.

Layer Examples Claim supported

19.2 Latest source checks

The first curated public export passed 136 tests with five skips on CPU job 6479723. Skips are pinned-tokenizer tests and deliberately excluded private corpora, not silently passed model tests. Final packaging changes were covered by seven targeted API, CPU-demo, data and packaging checks in a fresh isolated installation and local Git clone. Reporting tools were compiled/executed separately. The CPU UI browser check had no JavaScript errors and every returned answer was explicitly simulated. [E26, E27]

The public tree includes CI configuration for minimal CPU checks and model-logic tests. Configured CI is not executed remote CI. The clean source checkout cannot perform real inference or reproduce private prepared-data hashes without the required separately obtained artifacts. A locally cloned repository is not a verified clone from a published GitHub revision.

19.3 Environment separation

The recorded GPT-OSS adaptation/comparison overlay uses Python 3.10.19, PyTorch 2.8.0, Transformers 4.57.5, PEFT 0.18.1, Accelerate 1.12.0 and Numpy 2.2.6. A retained CPU/API environment uses PyTorch 2.6.0+cu124 and Numpy 1.26.4; the minimal demo environment does not require model weights or Torch. Native serving uses its qualified vLLM profile. The older generic optional extras are not instructions to install every incompatible framework profile together.

Every important GPU run should retain command, source identity, configuration, seed, model/data hashes, Slurm ID, GPU, hostname, timestamps and framework/CUDA versions. Original research used SHA256 snapshots because the handoff lacked usable Git history. New release commits do not retroactively become the commits used for old experiments. [E28]

20. Research release and publication pipeline

The local release candidate is a curated source-only repository named moe-routing-and-adaptation, with a local main branch and v1.0.0-rc.1 tag. It contains maintained code/configs/tests, public aggregate evidence, reports, figures, a clearly simulated CPU entry point and deployment/reproduction guides. The prior compact source package had 256 files and was approximately 714 KiB; this larger report is an additional deliverable and must be separately reconciled before publication rather than assumed present in that earlier ZIP.

Publication preparation replaces author-specific site paths and node names with templates, scans known credential patterns, checks the actual staged file list and verifies documentation links. Raw conversations, raw answer dumps, model weights, environments, private audits and original recovery archives are excluded. Known-pattern scanning is limited and does not prove arbitrary text contains no secret. Model/data rights remain separate from the code license.

GitHub SSH authenticates as raman-gatech; at the last verified remote check the new repository did not exist and API creation credentials were unavailable. The user was asked to create an empty remote. No publication URL, successful push, remote CI or release upload is fabricated. The narrated real-model walkthrough also remains pending. Existing real browser screenshots are integration evidence, not a narrated video or current live endpoint.

21. Evidence-backed conclusions, limitations and threats to validity

21.1 Conclusions supported by the artifacts

  • The external artifact set was recovered/preserved and the maintained runtime uses validated named adapter selection rather than the original mismatch.
  • Stage 2 trained nonzero attention updates, preserved resume state and produced an independently restorable, numerically qualified standard research artifact.
  • Actual native FFN adapter state and optional gate values changed in both relevant Stage 3 pilots; the later best checkpoints are trained states.
  • A declared calibration produced a passing standard Stage 3 export without relaxing the original numerical threshold.
  • The frozen comparison has 1,500 identity-checked outputs and exact paired input equality; its automatic proxies do not favor the selected update.
  • Restricted application checks succeeded, while operating and quality failures remain explicitly failed. The latest service is stopped.

21.2 What is not established

There is no independently human-reviewed whole-suite accuracy/safety result, clinical validation, robust multi-seed improvement, semantic/pretraining decontamination, general numerical equivalence over arbitrary prompts, or exact Stage 3 serving-engine qualification. There is no newly pretrained foundation model, claim that native experts acquired named human-interpretable domains, or proof that fine-tuning cannot improve under a future justified design.

Single-seed short pilots limit generalization. Five export probes provide limited coverage. Selection on a small development set can overfit its target style. Quantization/dequantization/merge change numerical representations. Automatic matchers are imperfect and attributed reviewers may be biased. Prompt budgets and instructions confound the baseline-to-precision comparison. Reference answers can be wrong or underspecified. Latency results depend on workload and hardware. Historical notes can be stale, so current assertions use exact artifacts and the scheduler rather than the most optimistic document paragraph.

21.3 Interpretation of the negative result

Lower supervised NLL can coexist with worse generated-answer proxies. The observed evidence does not identify a unique cause: distribution mismatch, short adaptation, calibration/rounding effects and sample variability are possible hypotheses, not experimentally established explanations here. The responsible outcome is to retain the candidate as a research artifact and withhold promotion. No additional tuning on these held-out answers is planned.

Remaining item Dependency Completion evidence required
Independent answer/intent review Attributed reviewers and frozen rubric/sample Entered scores, disagreements/adjudication, valid denominators
Quality gate closure for production Separate future decision; current release is research-only New evidence satisfying actual gates; no waiver from packaging
Latest cold-start reliability No new model experiment is required by this report A separately authorized/justified release-verification result; latest miss stays retained

Narrated walkthrough Verified accessible exact-profile demo or clearly historical material Credential-safe recording labelled with profile, date and limitations

Full independent review is preferred. If a fixed stratified subset is reviewed, its sample and rubric must be declared before scoring and its limited scope reported. A publisher label cannot substitute for prompt-intent adjudication. Reviewers should score correctness, relevance, completeness, refusal behavior and unsupported claims separately and preserve uncertainty. AI review is not relabeled human review. No training is part of completing documentation.

The project is complete as a bounded research experiment and substantial engineering implementation. The research source release is prepared locally. Production quality and independent validation are incomplete. Those statements can all be true at once; the final report preserves that distinction.

Appendix B. Saved training and routing figures

Curves are derived from the two saved 200-row metric files; no missing historical Stage 2 learning curve is fabricated.

Each layer's counts pool the five recorded sources and normalize by its observed assignments. Similar heatmaps do not establish equal quality, causal gate effects, semantic expert labels or general load balancing. Raw telemetry and derivation identities are listed in the evidence catalog.

The screenshot is historical real-model integration evidence. Its “ready” badge is not a current readiness claim. The allocation subsequently stopped.

Appendix E. Reproduction and reporting boundaries

The source CPU quick start is python -m pip install -e '.[dev]' followed by the targeted API/demo/data/packaging tests. The release also provides an exact CPU-demo dependency lock. Real GPU inference requires the matching upstream base, compatible tokenizer/adapters, separate model access, a qualified environment and an actual allocation. Full past research requires identity-matched prepared data and archived artifacts; a source-only clone does not supply them.

Read-only status verification uses squeue, sacct, exact job-bound reports and artifact checksums. Do not execute historical training/export commands merely because they are documented: experimentation is frozen. To rebuild this report, run scripts/build_comprehensive_diagrams.py and scripts/complete_comprehensive_report.py, then render the Markdown with the report renderer. Rebuilding uses saved evidence and creates no model experiment.

Some underlying metrics were generated by preexisting imperfect automatic scorers; the report preserves their limitations and versions. It does not fabricate human labels, silently relax thresholds, merge incompatible cohorts or convert a clean scheduler exit into a quality pass. Updated publication/deployment evidence should be appended with a new verification timestamp, preserving prior failed records.
